# @amelhede/rppg-web (test build of @elata-biosciences/rppg-web, Elata main as of 2026-07-26 = 0.14.0 plus Elata's unreleased changes): context for tools and agents

Test build: five heart-rate fixes, one speed change and a real-pulse check, each behind a switch, all ON by default (`fixes`, `pulseCheck`, `pulseCheckRules` on `createRppgSession`). Install with an npm alias so imports stay `@elata-biosciences/rppg-web`. See README "Switches".

## Role
Browser **rPPG** (camera photoplethysmography): WASM backend, optional MediaPipe face ROI, BPM / metrics. **Primary entrypoint: `createRppgSession()`**. Higher-level UI/gating: **`createRppgAppAdapter()`**, **`createRppgAppMonitor()`**; auto-retry failures: **`createManagedRppgSession()`**. Lower-level: **`RppgProcessor`**, **`DemoRunner`**, frame sources.

## Requirements
- **Node.js >= 20** for tooling. Browser: WebAssembly; camera via `getUserMedia` where applicable.
- Published tarball includes **`dist/`** and **`pkg/`** (WASM). Local **`file:`** installs copy disk at install time: run `build:wasm` in the repo **before** installing if `pkg/` is missing.

## Critical: WASM loading (especially Vite)
Default loader fetches **`/pkg/rppg_wasm.js`** and **`.wasm`**. If the backend never loads (also: a build deployed under a sub-path, since these URLs are root-absolute), **`backendMode` is `"unavailable"`**, the engine falls back to its JavaScript estimators (with `pulseCheck: false` a rate still comes, off the build's measured path; with the pulse check on, its rate can still come), **`onError`** fires with code **`backend_init_failed`** (each URL tried and the error it failed with in `session.lastError.message`), and **`getState()`** reads `degraded`. With `backend: "wasm"` the session throws instead.

Fixes (see README): copy `node_modules/.../rppg-web/pkg/` to **`public/pkg/`**, or use **`wasmImporter`** with a static import of `pkg/rppg_wasm.js`, or **`wasmJsUrl` / `wasmBinaryUrl`** with Vite **`?url`** imports. Vite 7 may block dynamic imports from `/public`: do not assume copying to `public/` is enough without the README patterns.

## Pulse check
- `pulseCheck` (on by default): a rate is reported only while forehead and both cheeks prove one pulse; `session.getPulseCheck()` shows its state.
- `foreheadPool` (session option, off by default; needs `pulseCheck`): the forehead region is read from 49 small skin patches weighted toward the cleanest instead of one box; the cheeks stay boxes. `getBuildSwitches().foreheadPool` reports it.
- `light` (session option, off by default; needs `pulseCheck`): `session.light()` gives how much light the screen should put on the face, 1 from the first frame of the measurement, or 0.5 once if rendered full light burns the face out for 2 s, never back; the app renders what it can and calls `session.reportLight(level)`; ignoring it leaves the reading unchanged. `getBuildSwitches().light` reports it.
- `pulseCheckRules`, each on unless set to false (`getBuildSwitches()` reports them): `screenLight` (a window in which one light steps on the forehead and both cheeks alike 10 or more times, such as a screen showing video, does not count toward the proof; slow or shallow screen changes are still missed), `restBand`: a line from 52 to 57 a minute counts with two of the three regions instead of every region if it also reaches -2 dB (more readings at a slow resting rate; off, the 58 edge). OFF unless true (being measured): a rate the room (the frame's upper corners) carries withheld. `moreReadings`, OFF unless true but on by default in a session with the face mesh ( merged in test.51 from `showBuilding` and `relock`): while no pulse is proven, a streak of 4 counting windows at -5 dB or more is shown at its mean rate (`getPulseCheck().buildingBpm`, `shownPulseBpm(state)`), and a 2-window streak at -4 dB or more within 6 bpm of a rate proven in the last 30 s is that rate again; it shows more numbers on real photos than the check without it, so it needs a liveness check first. `blinkGate`, OFF unless true but on by default in a session with the face mesh: no rate until the eyes have blinked once since the face appeared (a photo does not blink); a video of a face on a screen is not caught. `coherentFusion`, on unless false: the line from the regions' pulses added in time instead of their spectra added, and a building number from 3 agreeing windows. `shortStreak`, on unless false: with `moreReadings`, the building number from 2 agreeing windows. `followRecent`, on unless false: while nothing shows, a window rate within 6 bpm of a number proven in the last 60 s, at -5 dB or more, is shown (`getPulseCheck().followBpm`); it follows proven numbers only. `steadyLight`, on unless false: with `moreReadings`, the building number waits while its window holds 3 or more light steps. `roomLight`, on unless false: a rate the room (the frame's upper corners) carries is withheld. `clearWindows`, on unless false: with `moreReadings`, the building number counts only windows whose line stands 3 dB above any other peak 15 bpm or more away; pair it with `new PulseDisplay({ recentMs: 20000 })`. `coherentStart`, on unless false: a new number (none shown in the last 30 s) shows only when at least half the window rates of the last 30 s lie within 6 bpm of it (`getPulseCheck().startGated`). `oneRegion`, on unless false: a window counts toward the proof when one region carries its line instead of two (more readings at a wearable's accuracy; more numbers on no-pulse copies). `headMotion`, on unless false: a rate the moving head keeps time with (or half of it, a walk's stride) is not a pulse, so a walk's step rate never shows as a heart rate. `driftLine`, on unless false: a line under 52 a minute that fewer than three regions carry (it can count under no rule) no longer hides the pulse; the window reads its strongest line at 58 or above. `lightTaint`, on unless false: a window whose rate the wall beside the face carries never counts toward a streak (a lamp's flicker is not a pulse). `quickerProof`, on unless false: in the dark (a camera slowed to 15 to 18 fps) a proof from 12 agreeing windows at -5 dB instead of 16 at -4.5, and a streak longer than 8 windows also proves when its newest 8 average -3 dB. `keptFollow`, on unless false, acts with `followRecent`: across a break (the page left to read a watch) the rate proven before it stays the follow's anchor until the check proves again (at most 60 s old, two regions, -3 dB), and a blink seen before a break of at most 45 s still opens the refill. `movingFollow`, on unless false, acts with `followRecent`: while the head moves, a window follows the shown number at 2 dB under the usual bar. `bridgeGap`, on unless false: frames that stop for at most 2.5 s with the same face on both sides (centre within 0.3 face widths, width within 20%) are a freeze, not a break: the check and the analysis read across the hole instead of starting over (a camera that stalls no longer costs a whole window of collecting at every stall). `heldFrames`, on unless false: a window in which a tenth or more of the frames repeat the frame before in runs of 4 or more (a video encoder's held picture, such as a low-bitrate call stream) is not evidence of a pulse, and nothing shows or follows on it. `slowDouble`, on unless false: a line at twice a slow line (30 to 47 a minute) that the spectrum itself supports, a heart under the band's second harmonic, is withheld instead of shown as the double; it never shows a slow rate. On unless false: `allPatches` (the line from the 115 face patches instead of the three regions). Off unless true: `skinFallback` (off unless true: a face patch or region whose fixed skin-colour test keeps under half its pixels is read from all its pixels), `fpsCeiling` (a line above 0.4 times the window's frame rate is not a line), `tracker` (off unless true: one model, a filter over heart rates with a no-pulse state, decides the number in place of the streak rules).
- `PulseDisplay`: push `shownPulseBpm(state)` or null each second; `view(now)` is `measuring`, `live` (median of the last 5 s of numbers), `recent` (no new number for 5 to 10 s, show greyed) or `last` (older, with `agoS`). Changes no reading. `new PulseDisplay({ showEveryMs: PULSE_DISPLAY_SHOW_EVERY_MS })`: the number changes at most every 5 s. Off unless set: `medianMs` (median length, 5000 by default, 0 the newest number alone), `hystBpm` (the number changes only by hystBpm or more, or by less held for 3 s).
- `slowSwitch` (session option, off unless set): under 9 analysed frames a second in 5 whole seconds in a row (face tracked, page visible, after 3 s) the session moves the face finder to its worker and the check to rules `tracker` and `allPatches`, once, and calls `onSlowSwitch(record)`; `{ remembered: true }` starts switched; `getSlowSwitch()` gives `{ at_s, fps_before, fps_after_10s, remembered }`; a recording keeps it as an `"s"` event.
- `pulseCheckCause(state, faceInView)`: why no number (`collecting` while the 16 s window fills after a start or reset, then `noRate`, `weakSignal`, `agreeing`, ...); `pulseCheckColourDamaged(state)`: name light as the fix for a weak signal on a lit face only when this is true.
- `recordPulseCheckInputs` (off by default; `true` or `{ seconds }`): the session keeps what the pulse check was fed and every `getMetrics()` read, newest 5 minutes by default (about 7 MB at 30 frames a second). `session.getPulseCheckRecording()`, saved with `serializePulseCheckRecording` and read back with `parsePulseCheckRecording`, replays offline through the same check with any `pulseCheckRules` via `replayPulseCheck(recording, { rules })`; with the recording's own rules and `dropped: 0` every read's `bpm` equals the rate the session showed. Recording changes no output.

## Session behavior
- Framing: the app adapter withholds the rate and says "Move a little closer" only while the padded face box is under **0.12** of the frame width (`DEFAULT_FRAMING_THRESHOLDS`, measured: the face finder loses a face at about 0.10, and from 0.10 to 0.12 some faces read far less often; 0.14.0 used 0.34, which held normal laptop distances at "move closer" with no number). `PUBLISHED_FRAMING_THRESHOLDS` via `gating.framingThresholds` restores 0.14.0. `gating.framingAdvice: true` (off by default) keeps the rate for a mis-framed face and gives the framing message as advice (measured: off-centre and close faces in the frame read with no wrong second); no face still withholds. A head box taller than 0.8 of the frame (`maxHeight`, measured) gets "move back" as advice only, the rate kept. The "move closer" floor is judged against the frame's longer side (`longSide`), so portrait frames (a phone held upright) are judged like landscape ones in pixels.
- Expect **20 to 40 s** of a still, lit face before the first BPM (the pulse check shows a rate only once the face regions agree on it); meanwhile diagnostics often include **`insufficient_window`**.
- Check **`diagnostics.state`**, **`backendMode`**, and **`faceTrackingMode`** (`face_mesh` vs `video_frame` when `faceMesh: "auto"`).
- In `face_mesh` mode a frame with no face is dropped (`no_face`, `roiSource` null); after **1 s** with no face `getMetrics()` reports no reading (**`bpm: null`**, every estimate and window figure cleared as for a failed backend, reason `no_face`, baseline and calibration kept), and the sample window and engine pipeline restart when the face returns. `requireFace: false` restores the old centre-of-frame read.
- ROI behavior is versioned and composable. Omit `roiGeometryProfile` and `roiPixelSampler` for existing SDK behavior. Use `MCD_PROXY_INPUT_V1_PROFILE` only for the frozen model-input geometry, `TRADELOCK_LIVE_FOREHEAD_V1_PROFILE` for live-pipeline replay, and `TRADELOCK_RGB_WEIGHTED_V1_PIXEL_SAMPLER` for TradeLock pixel-selection replay. Do not treat those two geometry profiles as interchangeable.
- `sampleRppgRoi()` produces `elata.rppg.roi-sample/v1`, including raw and compatibility skin fractions plus geometry/sampler IDs for traceability.
- Bayesian ambiguity penalties are off by default. Opt in with a validated `elata.rppg.bpm-tracker-config/v1`; diagnostics expose the config ID and applied penalty.
- External evidence-quality models belong behind `BpmEvidenceQualityProvider`; SDK bounds all outputs and treats failures as neutral.
- Waveform reconstruction is diagnostic and opt-in through `experimental.waveformReconstructor`; it remains off the frame path and cannot feed BPM (`useReconstructedBpmEvidence` only accepts `false`).
- `extractWaveformMorphology()` exposes gated, source-labelled cycle features; any physiological trend proxy remains under `experimentalProxies`.
- `normalizePhysiologyFeatures()` has no labels. `createPhysiologyInterpreter()` adds generic policy-free states; its activation score is distinct from face affect, emotional valence, stress, and clinical interpretation.

## Related
If a project uses both **`rppg-web`** and **`eeg-web`**, prefer **matching published versions** unless release notes say otherwise.

## Source of truth
https://github.com/AMelhede/elata-bio-sdk/tree/release/test-1/packages/rppg-web (upstream: https://github.com/Elata-Biosciences/elata-bio-sdk)

Experimental, off by default: `experimentalVitals: true` on createRppgSession hands over HRV and breathing (from chest and shoulder motion below the chin) in their own box, `session.getExperimentalVitals()` returns `{ experimental: true, hrvRmssd, breathing }` or null. For research and testing, not measurements. Separate from `respiration_rate`, which stays withheld with the pulse check on. With `experimentalHrv: "tracking"` (pulse check on), `hrvRmssd` comes from the tracking-band beat timer `hrvFromRegions` on the check's three face regions over the latest 60 s, gated on window SNR >= 1 dB, its window in `hrvTracking`; default `"engine"`, the engine's HRV.
- Around the number (also from `@elata-biosciences/rppg-web/guide` and `/camera`): `PulseGuide` with `session.getGuideInput()` gives the one instruction to show, only when the person must act; `PULSE_DISPLAY_RECOMMENDED` for `PulseDisplay`; `rememberRate` (on unless false) and `getLastReading()` with `PulseDisplay.setLast`; `pulseCheckResume` across a camera restart; `keepScreenOn`, `isGreyFrame`/`otherCamera`, `hdFallback`, `watchCameraReturn`.
- `passive`, off unless set (session option): a second, passive lane for when nobody waits. Every 5 s it reads the last 48 s only if the line clears -6 dB, the two 24 s halves agree within 3 bpm and the newest 16 s agrees within 3 bpm; `session.passiveReading()` or `onPassiveReading` give the reading with its age. A 48 s average for resting rate and trends, never the live number; the live check is unchanged.
